items.title: BPS black holes in flat space from quantum mechanics
items.abstract: Despite extensive work on BPS black holes in 4d flat space, there is no direct microstate counting from D-brane quantum mechanics in regimes described by Einstein gravity. We derive an exact formula counting BPS configurations of the D-brane system corresponding to black holes in $N=8$ supergravity obtained from type II strings on $T^6$. As part of the derivation, we relate the BPS equations to a solvable modified Calogero-Moser system. The result agrees with the prediction from the modified elliptic genus of the D1-D5 system, providing a highly nontrivial test of the string dualities relating the two descriptions. We emphasize that this quantum mechanical system is, as a model of quantum black holes, simpler than BFSS and propose some numerical tests to explore this.

items.title: Separation of gravitational perturbations of singly spinning Myers-Perry black holes
items.abstract: Gravitational perturbations of rotating black holes in higher dimensions generally obey coupled partial differential equations. We show that scalar gravitational perturbations invariant under rotations of the transverse sphere of a singly spinning Myers-Perry black hole separate, despite the obstruction to a decoupled Teukolsky equation. Two commuting, second-order angular operators organise the three gauge-invariant curvature components into joint eigenfunctions. The physical radial problem is a $2\times2$ first-order system, equivalent to a single second-order equation. This gives a separation of the sector containing both the bar-mode and axisymmetric ultraspinning instabilities. Using only ordinary differential equations, we compute the bar-mode quasinormal spectrum in $d=5,6,7$ and find instability onsets at $a/r_+=0.90498$ and $0.83228$ in $d=6,7$. We also compute the growing axisymmetric modes and their onset rotations in $d=6,\ldots,9$. The construction shows how separability can survive the coupling between gravitational polarisations.

items.title: Arithmetic of Duality Defects in 4d Maxwell Theory
items.authors: Damian van de Heisteeg, Ling Lin, Giacomo Maggiorotti
items.abstract: We study the arithmetic structure of non-invertible duality defects in 4d $U(1)$ Maxwell theory. First, we recast the problem of realizing an elliptic $SL(2,\mathbb{Q})$ transformation as a duality defect in terms of complex multiplication for two-tori. The resulting classification includes well-studied cases in the literature, but extends to infinite Diophantine families of defects at a given gauge coupling. Second, we describe their worldvolume theories explicitly, with the Chern--Simons couplings determined by using continued fractions and tridiagonal continuant matrices. Third, we work out the fusion products of these defects, extracting the condensation defects and decoupled sectors both by lattice arithmetic and from the worldvolume descriptions. Finally, we illustrate our findings with the familiar $N$-ality defects (with $N=2,3$), but also give examples of infinite order.

items.title: The simplest event shape in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills
items.abstract: We study two-point event shapes in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills, with source, sink and detectors given in terms of half-BPS scalars and their light transforms. Akin to local correlation functions, at order by order in perturbation theory, in the large charge limit, this event shape factorizes into the product of two octagons evaluated on the unit circle. Borrowing the octagon results, we study its behavior with respect to the coupling and the angle between the detectors.

items.title: Thermal Giant Graviton Expansion
items.abstract: We construct giant graviton expansions of the thermal and $(-1)^F$-graded partition functions of $\mathcal{N}=4$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Yang-Mills theories at zero 't Hooft coupling. These observables are generically non-BPS and do not admit a direct bulk interpretation in a supergravity regime. Instead, we exploit the corresponding self-dual theories, which arise as chiral zero-coupling limits and admit twistor string holographic duals. We apply a quiver generalization of Murthy's expansion motivated by twistor strings. Notably, we obtain expansions at both finite and infinite $N$. We reproduce the terms in these expansions from bulk closed string and D-brane sectors, identifying the nonperturbative corrections with D-instanton/anti-D-instanton pairs. At infinite $N$, resumming the D-instanton sectors reproduces the Hagedorn temperatures of the free gauge theories, providing a microscopic bulk origin for their Hagedorn singularities.

items.title: Monopoles on the edge
items.abstract: Quantum M2-brane instantons are studied in eleven-dimensional Freund-Rubin backgrounds. The construction uses the identification of the Calabi-Yau cone over the Sasaki-Einstein manifold $\mathrm{SE}_7$ with the geometric branch of the abelian moduli space of the dual superconformal field theory. A class of BPS cycles in $\mathrm{SE}_7$ wrapped by M2-branes is identified as links of two-dimensional holomorphic cones whose coordinate rings contain BPS monopole operators. The algebraic structure and R-charge assignment on the moduli space further allow the computation of both the classical exponents and one-loop partition functions of the corresponding M2-brane instantons. Several three-dimensional superconformal field theories are analysed explicitly, and the relation to the corresponding localisation matrix models is discussed.

items.title: Coherent states of neutrinos in rotating matter
items.abstract: We study coherent states of neutrinos electroweakly interacting with rotating matter. We start with the Dirac equation for a massive neutrino propagating in background matter with a coordinate dependent effective potential. Then, we consider the limit of massless particles and the specific matter velocity profile. It allows us to reduce the neutrino Hamiltonian to the harmonic oscillator form. We find the exact solutions of the Dirac equation and construct the creation and annihilation operators. Using these results, we build the generalized coherent states of neutrinos. We provide the interpretation of these coherent states in terms of the classical physics. In particular, we demonstrate that the coherent states constructed approach plane waves in the limit of slow matter rotation. We also define the effective neutrino mass owing to the interaction of a massless neutrino with rotating matter. Then, we consider a special case of the generalized coherent states which are called the neutrino coherent states. The situation of the degenerate parameters of the system is also studied. Finally, we apply our results for astrophysical neutrinos propagating in dense matter of a rapidly rotating neutron star (NS). We calculate the effective neutrino masses for different neutrino energies for realistic parameters of NS.

items.title: Kinetic Equations and Turbulence in Large $N$ Vector and SYK-like Models
items.abstract: We apply large $N$ expansion techniques to derive kinetic equations for strongly coupled, far-from-equilibrium field theories with $O(N)$ symmetry. For large $N$ vector models, the quasi-classical approximation holds. Incorporating arbitrary momentum-dependent interactions, we show the dynamics obey the standard kinetic equation, with the scattering amplitude given by the retarded propagator of the auxiliary Hubbard-Stratonovich field. This has broad applications to systems like spin wave and Langmuir ion-acoustic turbulence. For large $N$ random coupling (SYK-like) models in $d$ dimensions, leading-order melon diagrams induce order-one propagator renormalization and finite spectral width. The corresponding kinetic equation, unlike those for standard weakly interacting systems, does not have a local-in-time collision integral. We find evidence for a stationary, scale-invariant infrared solution, revealing a potentially novel strong turbulence scaling exponent.

items.title: Infrared-Finite Positivity Bounds in 4D Gravity
items.abstract: We formulate an S-matrix bootstrap in an exactly flat half-space, where boundary reflection provides geometric infrared control for four-dimensional gravity. Under the channel positivity conditions, we obtain an infrared-finite positivity bound on local four-scalar Wilson coefficients that includes a finite gravitational correction of order $G_N$ and is derived from the full UV absorptive spectrum without specifying a UV theory, imposing a spectral ansatz, requiring weak coupling or expanding the spectrum perturbatively. At fixed dimensionless external state parameters, the coefficient of the leading gravitational correction is independent of the EFT scale and requires neither an arbitrary soft resolution scale nor a model-dependent UV scale. Gaussian wave-packet scattering localizes interactions within the flat region and directly probes bulk Wilson coefficients while exponentially suppressing sensitivity to the boundary. Long-range gravitons remain sensitive to the boundary and give a finite contribution. The smearing functional passes numerical positivity tests with general half-space absorptive kernels in both crossed channels. An explicit string example shows how boundary reflection suppresses the collective contribution of string resonances to the absorptive part of the amplitude, connecting infrared control of low-energy scattering to the UV spectrum of quantum gravity in the same dispersion relation. The framework opens a route to infrared-finite constraints on effective interactions across particle physics and gravity.

items.title: One-Loop Renormalization of Spin-$1/2$ SOPHIES
items.authors: I. D\'iaz-Saldan\~na, A. Guti\'errez-Rodr\'iguez, Armando de la C. Rangel-Pantoja, Carlos A. Vaquera-Araujo
items.abstract: In this paper, three formulations of spin-$1/2$ Second-Order Pseudo-Hermitian quantum field theorIES (SOPHIES) are built from scratch from parity eigenstates. Pseudo-Hermiticity allows the unconstrained fields to satisfy either Fermi--Dirac or Bose--Einstein statistics, while self-conjugate Majorana-like fields are only compatible with Fermi--Dirac. The set of independent four dimension renormalizable self-interactions of the three theories are identified, and the one-loop renormalization of the unconstrained fermionic and bosonic theories coupled to an abelian gauge boson and enhanced with a Pauli term and including self-interactions is studied, together with the one-loop renormalization of the only independent quartic self-interaction of self-conjugate fields. The analysis leads to a rich set of Renormalization Group Equations with deep connections to known theories, like the Dirac formalism and the Klein--Gordon scalar through the fixed points of the Pauli coupling.

items.title: Quantum Residues and the Geometry of Perturbative/Non-perturbative Relations
items.abstract: We develop a systematic, Whitham-based construction of perturbative/non-perturbative (P/NP) relations for one-dimensional quantum mechanical systems admitting a genus-one WKB period description, and derive a higher-genus formulation under explicit regularity assumptions. We select external deformations that preserve the independent quantum residues and lift them by varying the internal moduli so that the independent perturbative quantum periods remain fixed. The Riemann bilinear identity then determines the induced evolution of the non-perturbative periods through local residue pairings and the inverse period Jacobian. At genus one, this reduces to a relation between the flow of the non-perturbative quantum period and the energy derivative with respect to the perturbative action, providing a constructive connection between the Rayleigh-Schr\"{o}dinger expansion and fluctuations around non-perturbative saddles. We recover known P/NP relations and derive extensions for explicitly coupling-dependent potentials, which we verify at the computed orders through independent perturbative and non-perturbative period calculations for quantum-corrected quartic and Jacobi elliptic examples.

items.title: Mutual Information of Measurement in Conformal Field Theories
items.authors: Israel Klich, Ravisankar Rajagopal, Diana Vaman
items.abstract: The mutual information of measurement of a local operator between two spatial regions characterizes the reduction in the uncertainty of measurement outcomes in one region given the outcome in the other. We study the R\'enyi-Shannon mutual information of measurement in conformal field theories (CFTs). Explicit calculations for scalar primaries and descendants in large $N$ CFTs are performed in the two extreme limits of the intervals being adjacent or largely separated. The results depend on only the cross ratio and the scaling dimension $\Delta$ of the operator being measured, with striking similarities to the mutual information of entanglement. We find a surprising quadratic dependence as $(\Delta-1/2)^2$ for adjacent intervals. This dependence superficially seems to violate the information processing inequality, which we discuss and resolve. We also offer a holographic interpretation of the mutual information of measurement.

items.title: Linear stability matrix and Lyapunov exponents for stationary spacetime
items.abstract: Lyapunov exponents characterize the average rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge and therefore provide a useful criterion for dynamical stability. In this work, we develop a general framework for analyzing Lyapunov exponents in stationary spacetimes and extend previous studies beyond circular orbits. For a generic stationary spacetime described by $g_{\mu\nu}(r,\theta)$, we show that the phase space relevant to linear perturbations is spanned by $(r,p_r,\theta,p_\theta)$ and the corresponding linear stability matrix has rank four. When the spacetime admits a rank-2 Killing tensor, the linear stability matrix can be reduced to a block-diagonal form, allowing the Lyapunov exponents to be obtained analytically. By imposing the appropriate constraint conditions, the formalism further yields the linear stability matrices and Lyapunov exponents for circular and spherical orbits. The validity of the method is illustrated by several representative examples, including the (inverted) harmonic oscillator, planar Kepler motion, and particle motion in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes. These results provide a unified framework for investigating the stability properties of particle orbits in both classical and relativistic dynamical systems.

items.title: Gauge-invariant nonperturbative Wilson action in quantum electrodynamics II
items.abstract: The gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG) is a formulation of the exact renormalization group for gauge theories that provides a renormalization group flow preserving the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity exactly. In this paper, we nonperturbatively solve the GFERG flow equation for the simplest nontrivial gauge-invariant Wilson action, introduced in a previous paper, for $D$-dimensional quantum electrodynamics with~$N_f$ flavors (for all~$D$, flavors are counted in units of four-component spinors). For $D=3$ and~$D=2$, a nontrivial infrared fixed point exists even for~$N_f=1$, and the structure of the critical exponents at the fixed point is qualitatively the same as that in the large-$N_f$ limit. We also obtain the gauge-field propagator in the continuum limit; for~$D=2$, it reproduces the dynamical mass of the Schwinger model within a few percent. To the best of our knowledge, apart from the large-$N_f$ approximation, this is the first example in which the Wilson renormalization group in a gauge theory is solved nonperturbatively while manifestly preserving gauge symmetry.

items.title: Nambu's Dynamics, Strings and Gravitized Quantum Theory
items.abstract: In this article we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory. String theory, according to this view, originates in foundations of quantum theory and Nambu's dynamics, which features in the non-perturbative definition of string theory in terms of a T-duality covariant and non-commutative formulation, called the metastring. Nambu's dynamics and the associated cubic and hypercubic objects also appear as the natural language for exploring the new observables and phenomena implied by a dynamical Born rule, including triple and higher order quantum interference, that can be investigated in experiments involving massive quantum probes, and that are also needed for direct empirical tests of the Born rule, a cornerstone of quantum theory.

items.title: Catalan polynomials for the Wishart-Laguerre $\beta$-ensemble
items.authors: Bei Kang, Lu-Yao Wang, Ke Wu, Wei-Zhong Zhao
items.abstract: By means of $W$-representation, we investigate the Wishart-Laguerre $\beta$-ensemble and present a compact expression for Catalan polynomials. For a special Nekrasov partition function associated with the Wishart-Laguerre $\beta$-ensemble, we show that it can be expressed as a exponential form of the special Catalan polynomials. Furthermore, we make a rule to calculate the Catalan polynomials by means of Feynman diagrams and present another expression for Catalan polynomials. We also establish the connection between certain Catalan polynomials and knot theory.

items.title: The stability of non-Abelian $A_4$ vortices in $SO(3)$ gauge theory
items.authors: Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Kazuya Murakami, Muneto Nitta, Ryo Yokokura
items.abstract: We study the linear energetic stability of non-Abelian vortices in an $SO(3)$ gauge-Higgs theory with residual gauge group $A_4$. In our previous work, we identified two families of such vortices associated with order-two and order-three elements of $A_4$, and found Bogomol'nyi--Prasad--Sommerfield-like behavior at special ratios of the Higgs and gauge-boson mass scales. Here, we investigate their stability against $SO(3)$ gauge and Higgs perturbations by analyzing the second order variation of the vortex tension using analytical and numerical methods. In particular, when all relevant mass scales are equal, we prove linear stability for all vortices in the order-three family. By contrast, at the same mass point, we prove that a vortex in the order-two family is unstable. Thus, although both vortex families exhibit Bogomol'nyi--Prasad--Sommerfield-like behavior in their reduced equations at this mass point, their stability properties in the full $SO(3)$ theory are qualitatively different.

items.title: Finite Modular Hamiltonians and Their Singular Limits
items.authors: Panyinyan Li, Jun Tao, Haitang Yang
items.abstract: Using the open solid torus as a finite parent, we revisit modular flow for spherical regions in conformal field theory. Its nonsingular angular evolution gives finite modular generators in a very simple form, while an exact conformal map to a cavity frame recovers the Rindler, CHM, and stationary-source ball constructions as singular limits. The same finite parent also provides a regular completion of the center obstruction in the complexified ball flow. Charged, Dirac, and inhomogeneous scalar examples are given.

items.title: Realisation of de Sitter space as an excited state in string theory
items.abstract: String theory is widely regarded as the only plausible candidate for a consistent UV-complete theory of quantum gravity. Cosmological observations suggest that our universe is undergoing accelerated expansion, pointing towards the presence of a small positive cosmological constant. Since de Sitter space is the maximally symmetric solution of Einstein's equations with a positive cosmological constant, understanding whether four-dimensional de Sitter space can be realized within string theory has become one of the central questions. Following a series of works that realize de Sitter space as an excited state---namely, as a Glauber--Sudarshan (GS) state in type IIB string theory---our goal has been to extend such a construction to heterotic string theories. Realizing de Sitter space as an excited state over a time-independent supersymmetric Minkowski background provides a mechanism for evading the vacuum-based no-go theorems that obstruct de Sitter solutions in string theory. Starting from a generic M-theory configuration, we obtain four-dimensional de Sitter space in the late-time limit of flat-slicing coordinates in both heterotic $SO(32)$ and heterotic $E_8 \times E_8$ theories through appropriate dynamical duality sequences. The corresponding GS state is constructed by evaluating the expectation value of the metric operator in M-theory using path-integral techniques. We analyse the conditions required for the existence of a well-defined effective field theory description of the setup and find that these conditions are equivalent to satisfying the null energy condition in a 3+1-dimensional FLRW cosmology. Furthermore, the de Sitter GS states are found to lie well within the temporal bound imposed by the Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture, rendering them as transient states. In the case of $E_8\times E_8$ theory, we also investigate implications arising from axion cosmology.

items.title: Black hole cohomologies in N=4 SYM
items.authors: Seunggyu Kim, Jehyun Lee, Siyul Lee, Jaewon Song
items.abstract: We systematically investigate BPS cohomologies of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory with gauge group SU$(N)$ with $N=2, 3, 4$, focusing primarily on the BMN sector. We find non-Coulomb graviton cohomologies for $N>2$. For $N>2$, the lightest black hole cohomology in the BMN sector always carries non-trivial $R$-charge and corresponds to the brane-fused type. Therefore, the `core' black holes without hair are `heavier'. We also find that a family of brane-fused cohomologies in $N=3$ is not lifted at the first quantum order. At a fixed charge sector, gravitons carry definite parity under charge conjugation. Up to the levels we have tested, every black hole cohomology either has opposite parity to that of gravitons or is lifted by quantum corrections. We conjecture that black hole cohomologies always carry parity opposite to gravitons in the same charge sector.

items.title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
items.abstract: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.

items.title: Giant Wilson loops from Fredholm determinants
items.authors: Ludvig Chen, Victor Mishnyakov, Konstantin Zarembo
items.abstract: We study large-k symmetric and antisymmetric Wilson loops in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. We represent their generating functions as Fredholm determinants built from the Hermite kernel weighted by a symbol function that encodes the representation. Using the integrable structure of the kernel, we systematically apply the Tracy-Widom approach to derive a closed system of integro-differential equations. The equations are then solved order by order in 1/N by a WKB ansatz, while keeping the symbol function general. We find a closed-form expression for the leading and subleading order contributions to the generating functions. Finally, specializing to the two representations, we perform the large-k saddle-point analysis and find the subleading contribution to the Wilson loop. Our results confirm the previously observed discrepancies with the dual D-brane description of giant Wilson loops.

items.title: Thermal AdS two-point functions and loop induced effective one-point vertices
items.abstract: We present a study of thermal two-point functions from Witten diagrams in thermal AdS$_{d+1}$, defined with the conformal boundary $S_\beta^1 \times \mathbb{R}^{d-1}$, with an aim to establish a connection between thermal CFT data and perturbative bulk dynamics. We analyze one-loop tadpole and bench diagrams arising from the cubic $\phi\phi\chi$ interaction in the bulk, segregating the different relative thermal winding sectors for the bench, and also extend the analysis to include quartic scalar contact diagrams with and without derivative interactions. We also analyze the spinning exchange thermal two-point function. Utilizing the split representation of bulk propagators and the method of images we reorganize the thermal Witten diagrams into the standard AdS integrals and obtain spectral and image-sum representations that make KMS periodicity of the correlators manifest. Additionally, we show possible position dependent effective one-point vertices of scalar and spinning fields in the bulk arising from the reduction of the coincident- point thermal bulk to bulk propagator loop, allowing tadpole-type diagrams to be reconstructed from effective local bulk interactions. The bench diagram however retains an intrinsically bi-local structure. We further investigate the thermal one-point coefficients and perturbative OPE data encoded in these thermal correlators, including contributions associated with anomalous dimensions. Finally, we examine their relation to thermal dispersion relations and the role of contributions that are not determined by discontinuity data alone. Our results provide a set of explicit bulk constructions for exploring the analytic structure of thermal CFT correlators and their connection to the thermal conformal bootstrap.

items.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
items.abstract: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using multipole expansion and re-summation techniques, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.

items.title: Heavy-Heavy-Light-Light correlators from holography on the worldsheet
items.authors: Mat\'ias Colaneri, Diego H. Correa, V\'ictor I. Giraldo-Rivera, Nicol\'as A. Ivanovich
items.abstract: We study correlation functions of light local operators and defect changing operators on the conformal line set by the 1/2 BPS Wilson line of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills. We consider the defect changing operators associated with geometrical and internal cusp angles, which at strong coupling have a large scaling dimension and back-react on the dual $AdS_2$ world-sheet. We set up a holographic computation of correlation functions, in which the light operators are described by fluctuations around the cusped classical string solution, so that correlators of two defect changing operators and an arbitrary number of light protected operators are obtained from the on-shell action of these fluctuations. We implement this prescription in detail for the case of certain 4-point functions, with two light and two defect changing operators. Finally, since for small cusp angles the defect changing operators become light, we manage to derive relations satisfied by integrated correlators of light operators, valid at any coupling. We verify these relations at strong coupling for both internal and geometrical cusps.
